title: Bind CCP2 schedules to full authorized identity
description:
Scope: schedule identity and ownership in /home/mark/Developer/lichen-workspace/project-LICHEN/spec/02b-ccp-receiver-aware.md and its exact-wire section. Define bounded encodings for the full authorized root identity, DODAG scope, schedule generation, regional plan/version, and PHY profile. Distinguish schedule authority, receiver identity, TX-grant owner, and forwarding signer. Specify the state-ownership tuple and validation order. Use pinned upstream Yggdrasil key/address literals for examples, not an IID-equality or SHA-512-native profile. No routing or identity implementation changes belong here.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Preserve full-key ownership and upstream address compatibility. Specify only the context needed by CCP2; reuse established identity and trust contracts rather than inventing another trust system.
acceptance_criteria: The specification gives exact identity/context fields and their ownership semantics. Independent worked examples reject wrong-root, wrong-DODAG, truncated-identity alias, and cross-generation substitution. Root/DODAG examples agree byte-for-byte with the pinned upstream address oracle. A forwarding signer cannot acquire root or receiver authority merely by authenticating an outer link frame.
